title: finding(fields): four cell renderers draw a value-INDEPENDENT face — `password`/`secret` mask, `vector`/`grid` print a literal, for every input including `null`
body:
Found while closing the `{}` column of the cell-renderer census (objectui#8596), by rendering all 53 registered field types through `getCellRenderer` against `[]`, `{}`, `''` and `null` on `4eb665bcf` — 212 cells. Out of that card's scope, filed rather than swept.

## What was measured

Four of the 53 registered types render **the same bytes for all four inputs**, and for a populated value too. Their cell face does not read the value at all:

| field type | `[]` | `{}` | `''` | `null` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `password` | the six-dot mask | the six-dot mask | the six-dot mask | the six-dot mask |
| `secret` | the six-dot mask | the six-dot mask | the six-dot mask | the six-dot mask |
| `vector` | `[Vector]` | `[Vector]` | `[Vector]` | `[Vector]` |
| `grid` | `[Grid]` | `[Grid]` | `[Grid]` | `[Grid]` |

Source: `getCellRenderer`'s `standardMap` in `packages/fields/src/index.tsx` registers all four as argument-less arrow components that ignore `value` entirely.

## Why it is a defect and not a shrug

This is the class objectui#8481 / objectui#8490 / objectui#8580 / objectui#8596 have been closing one column at a time: **a cell that asserts something the record never stored.**

- An **empty** `password` or `secret` column draws exactly what a **populated** one draws. On screen, a credential that was never set is indistinguishable from a credential that is set — for a reader, for a screen reader, and for anyone auditing which rows still need one. The mask is the correct face for a value that exists; it is not a face for the absence of one.
- `vector` and `grid` print a bracketed literal that is neither the stored value nor an affordance. `EmptyValue`'s accessible name is "No value", a statement that is TRUE for all four of these inputs on all four types, and none of them can say it.

Every other renderer in this package already answers `null` with the shared affordance; these four are the only ones that cannot.

## Suggested shape (not a ruling)

The narrow version is the same test the rest of the file already uses: nothing stored means the shared `EmptyValue`, and a value that IS stored keeps the face it has today — the mask for `password` / `secret`, the literal for `vector` / `grid`. That leaves the security posture untouched: the mask never becomes weaker, it just stops appearing where there is nothing to mask.

Worth checking against `packages/fields/src/__tests__/` before choosing, and worth confirming that no consumer depends on the mask always rendering (objectui#8440 touches the same two types from the copy side, and is a different subject).
